holidays.name: National Doctors' Day
holidays.description: A day to say thanks to the physicians who patch us up, often with red carnations, thank-you notes, and the occasional awkward hospital cafeteria cake.
holidays.origin: First observed in Winder, Georgia in 1933, chosen by Eudora Brown Almond to mark the anniversary of the first use of ether anesthesia in surgery by Dr. Crawford Long on March 30, 1842. The U.S. Congress formally designated it in 1990.
holidays.funFact: The red carnation is the official flower of the day, and the first Doctors' Day featured cards sent to doctors and flowers placed on the graves of deceased physicians.

holidays.name: National Turkey Neck Soup Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to simmering one of the most underrated poultry parts into a rich, hearty soup that grandmas have been bragging about for generations.
holidays.origin: Like many food holidays, it is an unofficial observance spread by food bloggers and social media calendars, celebrating a thrifty, soulful comfort-food tradition where every part of the bird gets its moment.
holidays.funFact: Turkey necks are packed with collagen and bone-marrow flavor, which is why they are prized for making deeply savory broth at a bargain price.

holidays.name: I Am in Control Day
holidays.description: A day to declare yourself the boss of your own life, or at least your own sock drawer. It encourages people to take charge of their choices and attitude.
holidays.origin: This self-empowerment observance is an unofficial holiday promoted through holiday calendars, designed to nudge people toward taking ownership of their day-to-day decisions.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists call the belief that you can influence your own outcomes an internal locus of control, and it is linked to greater resilience and motivation.

holidays.name: Take a Walk in a Park Day
holidays.description: A day for ditching the screen, lacing up your shoes, and strolling among trees, ducks, and suspiciously confident squirrels.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance falls in early spring, when the weather warms up and parks come alive, making it a natural time to encourage people to get outside and move.
holidays.funFact: Studies have shown that spending even 20 minutes in a natural setting can lower stress hormone levels like cortisol.

holidays.name: Pencil Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble wooden pencil, the original undo-friendly writing tool, with sharpening ceremonies and doodling strongly encouraged.
holidays.origin: Observed on March 30 in honor of the date in 1858 when Hymen Lipman received the first U.S. patent for attaching an eraser to the end of a pencil.
holidays.funFact: Lipman's patent was later declared invalid in court because combining two existing items was not considered a true invention, yet we all still use erasers on pencils today.
